first_impression.reaction: Googled 'get married in new zealand' because it's the cheap, close option on our list and I want to know what the catch is. The intro answers the question in two lines and says the rules are as at November 2026, so I know it's dated. Jumped to the FAQ: clear, with the 3 working days and 3 months numbers, and government links I can check. Hazards (earthquakes, volcanoes, tsunami, weather) are there with Smartraveller as the source, which I respect. Where it falls down: every cost is 'a fee applies' with no figure, and nothing tells me what Wedded Wonderland charges or whether they take a cut from the lodges.

journey.quote: This guide takes each step in the order you will meet it, with the rules as at November 2026.
journey.reaction: A date on the rules. That's what I look for. Good start.

journey.quote: Arrange the licence at least 3 working days before the wedding, as it expires after 3 months.
journey.reaction: Hard numbers I can put straight into a spreadsheet. And the government page is linked so I can check them.
Honest hedge, and it matches the recognition section. No overselling.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in New Zealand?
journey.quote: Before the wedding you apply for a marriage licence, which confirms it is legal for you to marry, and a fee applies.
journey.reaction: How much? This is a government fee, it's published. Same with the certificate and the Apostille. Four times this page says 'a fee applies' and never once gives a number. That's what I'd be checking on other sites.

journey.quote: When you arrive in New Zealand, you visit a registry office to sign a declaration before the ceremony, and the addresses are on the application form.
journey.reaction: This is the catch I was looking for and it's stated up front. Good. But does it need an appointment, how long does it take, and do we both have to go? If we're marrying in Glenorchy, which registry office is close?

journey.quote: The ceremony can only take place at the places you put on the application, so include a back-up venue.
journey.reaction: Useful and specific. Exactly the kind of trap I'd want flagged before I pay a deposit.

journey.quote: What does your fee include, and when is it paid?
journey.reaction: A guide telling me to grill suppliers on fees. Fair. Now ask yourselves the same question.

journey.section: When to get married in New Zealand
journey.quote: New Zealand has several active volcanoes, and alert levels can rise quickly, with evacuation ordered at short notice.
journey.reaction: Didn't expect a wedding business to put this in. Sourced and plain. Trust up.

journey.quote: Napier and Hastings were rebuilt in Art Deco style after the 1931 earthquake, which gives a reception a setting with real period character.
journey.reaction: The region section is tourism-brochure stuff. Nice facts, but nothing on how far each is from an airport, guest accommodation, or cost differences. 'Real period character' is mood, not information.

journey.quote: If you would like help weighing two regions against your guest list, ask Wedded Concierge.
journey.reaction: Sales link in the middle of a section that hasn't given me enough to weigh anything myself.

journey.quote: What drives the cost is the season, the number of nights you take the property, how many guests stay on site, how remote the setting is, and how much has to travel in.
journey.reaction: Cost drivers but not one range. Even a rough 'from AUD' for a lodge buyout would tell me whether this is realistic on our budget.

journey.quote: Deposits and contracts: whose name is on the contract, in which currency are payments made, and when do deposits become non-refundable?
journey.reaction: This is the question I got burned on last time. Good sign a planner raises it.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee agreed in writing is good. But 'payments' through you is exactly where I ask: do you take a cut from the lodge? Not answered. And no real New Zealand wedding with a budget anywhere.

journey.section: Plan your New Zealand wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Everything around it is where the planning begins.

turn_offs_found.quote: Before the wedding you apply for a marriage licence, which confirms it is legal for you to marry, and a fee applies.
turn_offs_found.why: Government fees are published, yet the page says 'a fee applies' for the licence, certificate and Apostille without a single figure. Unquantified costs look like the catch to someone building a budget.

turn_offs_found.quote: Napier and Hastings were rebuilt in Art Deco style after the 1931 earthquake, which gives a reception a setting with real period character.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional, brochure-style language in the region section instead of the practical facts I'd use to choose (airport access, travel time, accommodation).

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would like help weighing two regions against your guest list, ask Wedded Concierge.
turn_offs_found.why: CTA lands before the section has given enough evidence to compare regions myself.

turn_offs_found.quote: Everything around it is where the planning begins.
turn_offs_found.why: Mood line with no information, on a page that otherwise earns trust with facts.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the 3 working days / 3 months licence window, the named back-up venue rule and the Copy of Particulars vs certificate distinction, for our spreadsheet
Our Reddit thread: the celebrant questions and the lodge contract questions (whose name, which currency, when deposits go non-refundable)

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor stays with you from start to finish, works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after a lot of genuine, sourced evidence, and the promises are concrete (AUD quotes, inclusions in writing). But how the fee is worked out and whether you take a cut from lodges aren't answered, and there's no real wedding or budget to look at. I'd email those questions before booking a call.

top_3_changes: Fees: give the current licence, certificate and Apostille fees from the government sources with an 'as at' date (flagged for checking), or link the exact fee pages beside each 'a fee applies' sentence.

Registry office visit: state what the source says about whether both partners attend, whether it needs booking and where offices are relative to the main wedding regions; if the source doesn't say, write 'not published' and put it on the checklist.

Cut mood lines ('real period character', 'Everything around it is where the planning begins') and move the mid-region Concierge link down; if the source pack allows, add practical region facts like nearest airport instead.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, looked for the catch and the numbers, flagged unsupported or emotional language
No invented brand facts; fees, commissions, real weddings, ground team and Privileges listed as deferred unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Does the source pack hold the licence, certificate and Apostille fee amounts (fact_201, fact_03, fact_223) and any detail on the registry office visit (fact_206)? If yes, the fee and registry objections close with sourced lines; if not, 'not published' plus a direct link is the fallback.
